seoTitle: Paint Color Mixer: Blue and Yellow Make Green
metaDescription: Mix paint colours the way pigments behave, subtractively, and compare with a screen average. Free, local.
intro: Mixes paints with a Kubelka-Munk model so blue and yellow give green instead of grey.
why:
On screens colours add light, so averaging blue and yellow gives a grey. Paints absorb light, so mixing darkens and shifts hue. This tool converts each colour to absorption and scattering per channel, averages them by parts and converts back.

It is an illustration. Real paint depends on pigment, opacity and medium, and the tool has no measured spectra. Treat it as a hint, not a recipe.
howTo: Enter one paint colour per line, with parts after it.
Compare the pigment-style mix with the screen average.
Test your real paint on paper.
